claims.text: As-cast MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration material exhibits a large magnetocaloric effect.
As-cast MnNiSi-based material has limited fracture toughness and low yield strength.
Adding approximately 2 at.% Cu during arc melting and subsequently aging the alloy can produce nanoscale coherent Cu precipitates.
Homogenization followed by aging at approximately 600–650 °C for several hours promotes nucleation of the proposed Cu precipitates.
The resulting coherent Cu precipitates will be uniformly distributed both within grains and at grain boundaries.
Fine coherent Cu precipitates obstruct dislocation motion and thereby cause precipitation hardening.
The Cu precipitates act as barriers to crack propagation and delay crack initiation.
Obstruction of dislocation motion and delayed crack initiation enhance both yield strength and fracture toughness.
The Cu-doped and aged alloy will have 15–25% higher yield strength and fracture toughness than undoped MnNiSi.
Magnetic interactions primarily between Mn and Ni are responsible for the large magnetocaloric effect.
A limited volume fraction of coherent Cu precipitates will minimally disrupt the magnetic interactions responsible for the magnetocaloric effect.
The Cu-doped and aged alloy will retain a magnetocaloric effect of similar magnitude at the phase-transition temperature relative to undoped MnNiSi.
The mechanical benefit requires nanoscale coherent Cu precipitates rather than coarse or incoherent precipitates.
Excessive Cu addition or over-aging can generate coarse or incoherent precipitates.
Coarse or incoherent precipitates may degrade both mechanical properties and the magnetocaloric effect.
The proposed benefit applies only when processing preserves the magnetic ordering intrinsic to MnNiSi.

contradictions.description: The stated baseline is conventionally processed undoped MnNiSi, whereas the experimental control is undoped MnNiSi subjected to the same homogenization and aging treatment as the Cu-bearing alloy. These are potentially different baselines, so the comparison is not fully consistent.
